name: Acid Overdrive Line
description: After Attack Magazine's acid line: the bass-line synth's saw a sixteen-foot down through its own diode ladder, resonant and gliding a third of the way, into an overdrive and a ping-pong echo on the highs only. From the page: the octave, the glide at a third, the high resonance, the overdrive's 63 % drive and 60 % tone, the delay's 37 % feedback and 21 % wet; estimated: the cutoff and the envelope. Macro 1 (Cutoff) opens the ladder; Macro 2 (Accent) deepens the envelope; Macro 3 (Drive) pushes the overdrive.

name: Acid Squelch
description: A diode ladder bass that slides between overlapping notes.

name: Analog Wobble
description: A ladder opened and shut on eighth notes by the LFO.

name: Bassline Wub
description: After Syntorial's UK bassline: a sine bent by a sine three octaves up, a slow-attack envelope swelling the FM and the resonant low-pass into each note's wub, then a flanger opened by the same envelope, drive and chorus. From the page: the octaves, the amp's 65/368/0/52 ms, the envelope's 215 ms attack and 170 ms decay, its half depth on the FM and the cutoff, the half resonance; estimated: the effects' amounts. Macro 1 (Wub) deepens the envelope; Macro 2 (Flange) brings up the flanger; Macro 3 (Drive) pushes the shaper.

name: Brassy Lo-fi Bass
description: After Reverb Machine's lo-fi bedroom-pop breakdown: two saws eleven cents apart with noise at half, a brassy filter envelope opening each note slowly, a little tape wobble. From the page: the saws, the 11 cents (here either side of the note), the noise, the brassy envelope; estimated: its 60 ms attack and the cutoff, the wobble. Macro 1 (Brass) slows and deepens the swell; Macro 2 (Dust) brings the noise and the wobble up.

name: Buzzing Sub
description: After Future Music's huge sub bass on MusicRadar: a square that narrows toward a thin pulse, nudged by a 3.9 Hz LFO on its position, through a low-pass that follows the keys, mono, quick in and out. From the page: the square-to-eighth pulse table, the LFO's rate and small depth, the 374 Hz cutoff, 23 % resonance and 10 % drive, the 0.8 ms attack and 27 ms release; estimated: our pulse table's place for the page's frame (some way toward the thin pulse). Macro 1 (Buzz) narrows the pulse and drives the filter; Macro 2 (Wobble) deepens the LFO.

name: Chicago Pulse Bass
description: After a Chicago house bass tutorial: a pulse alone, mono, the filter shut and opened all the way by its envelope, which follows velocity and the keys, through a wet, slowish chorus. From the page: the pulse with no saw or sub, the cutoff at the bottom, the envelope at its full depth, velocity and keys at 70, the decay near 36 and the release near 33 on that synth's scale, the chorus near 90 % wet and just under half depth; estimated: the times in milliseconds. Macro 1 (Punch) deepens the envelope and its velocity; Macro 2 (Chorus) wets the chorus.

name: Click Organ Bass
description: After Jon Musgrave and Si Truss's classic house organ on MusicRadar: a triangle and a square a twelfth up (a fifth and an octave), mono, through a 24 dB low-pass that falls from about 2.5 kHz to 300 Hz, with a noise click through a fast envelope at each note, a little reverb and slap. From the page: the waves and the +19 semitones, the cutoff's fall, the filter decay near a fifth and its 40 % depth, the click's short envelope, the medium reverb and an eighth-note slap; estimated: the times. Macro 1 (Click) raises the noise click; Macro 2 (Bright) slows the cutoff's fall; Macro 3 (Space) brings up the reverb and slap.

name: Clipped Boom
description: After EDMProd's trap sub bass: one sine two octaves down, a short envelope diving its pitch into each note, gliding between overlapping notes, clipped hard. From the page: the single voice, the sine, the octave, the reset phase, the pitch envelope, the soft clip at about 17 dB; estimated: the dive's depth (an octave here), its 70 ms decay, the glide. Macro 1 (Dirt) drives the clip harder; Macro 2 (Punch) deepens the pitch dive; Macro 3 (Glide) lengthens the slide.

name: Counter Neuro Bass
description: After Attack Magazine's twisted neuro bass: two tables an octave and two octaves down moving the opposite ways on one bar-long LFO, the second bent, through a band-reject the LFO sweeps, gliding, with some noise, then a heavy drive, chorus and a frequency shifter. From the page: the octaves (10 cents apart, here either side of the note), the positions (45 % and 40 %), the bend just past half, the notch near a quarter, the glide, the noise at a third, the LFO's -0.33, +0.33 and half to the notch, the drive's 60 % wet; estimated: our tables, the shifter's amount. Macro 1 (Shift) brings in the shifter; Macro 2 (Notch) sharpens the notch; Macro 3 (Motion) deepens the LFO.

name: Curious Bass
description: From Curiosity as part of the Forms Soundtrack

name: Deep House Bass
description: After Adam Douglas's house bass for Attack Magazine: a saw, a square at three quarters and a sub at near half through a half-open low-pass with a little resonance and raised key tracking, the envelope plucking it and narrowing the square, then the slowest chorus and a room. From the page: the levels, the envelope (not the LFO) on the width at 75 %, the cutoff at half, the filter decay near 15 % with no sustain, the amp's decay near half and sustain near a quarter; estimated: the times. Macro 1 (Pluck) deepens the envelope; Macro 2 (Width) narrows the square further; Macro 3 (Room) widens the room.

name: Dotted Warp Bass
description: After Attack Magazine's warping bass: a bent table over a square and a sine two octaves down, a sine LFO in dotted eighths (three sixteenths) restarted at each note on a resonant low-pass, then a comb in series, chorus and a small dense reverb. From the page: the bend, the table near 75 %, the octaves, the 3/16 rate, the cutoff and resonance near a quarter, the comb, the glide, the effects' 50 % and 30 %; estimated: the depths. Macro 1 (Comb) sweeps the comb's pitch; Macro 2 (Rate) speeds the LFO; Macro 3 (Space) widens the reverb.

name: Drawn Wobble
description: A wobble whose LFO is drawn, synced to eighths through the Two-Filter Mono's peaked low-pass; Macro 1 speeds it up.

name: Fat Ladder Bass
description: Two saws an octave apart and a sub through the transistor ladder.

name: Fifth Stack Bass
description: After Attack Magazine's jump-up stab bass: three saws, on the root, a fifth up and a nineteenth up (the top loudest), a nearly shut low-pass thrown open by a short envelope and following the keys, an FM edge swelling in, then a near-full waveshaper. From the page: the intervals and levels (0.32, 0.32, full), the retrigger, the cutoff near 10 % with some drive, the envelope's 70 %, the key tracking's 35 %, the FM's slow open; estimated: the decay (250 ms), the swell (30 ms). Macro 1 (Punch) deepens the envelope; Macro 2 (Bite) brings the FM edge in; Macro 3 (Drive) pushes the shaper.

name: FM Growl
description: The FM table's middle bent further by its own FM, the position on an LFO.

name: FM Neuro Bass
description: After EDMProd's neuro bass: a sine bent by a silent saw, a sine sub, a little noise worked by the LFO, through a dirty low-pass the LFO sweeps, the saw stepped in and out of sync, then a soft clip at 15 dB. From the page: the oscillators and their levels, the FM, the noise, the LFO on the filter and the noise, the 15 dB clip; estimated: the depths and the drawn LFO in quarters. Macro 1 (FM) deepens the bend; Macro 2 (Sync) moves the saw's sync; Macro 3 (Dirt) drives the filter.

name: Folded Tech Bass
description: After Attack Magazine's tech house bass: a saw-pulse and a pulse an octave down, a little feedback, the filter nearly shut and plucked open with low sustain, a wavefolder with its teeth up, and a short chorus-echo in sixteenths. From the page: the octave, the cutoff, the filter decay near a third with no sustain, the amp's sustain under a quarter, the light fold, the echo's sixteenths and low mix; estimated: our fold warp for the page's folder, the times. Macro 1 (Fold) folds deeper; Macro 2 (Pluck) deepens the envelope; Macro 3 (Echo) brings up the echo.

name: Formant Growl
description: After Preset Drive's heavy growl: a formant table bent by a second an octave above it, a triangle LFO in half notes walking the table and a sine in eighths the FM, a resonant low-pass, then a fold and a down-sampler. From the page: the table near 40 %, the 30 % FM, the octave, the LFOs' shapes and rates, the cutoff near half, the fold's half and the down-sampler's fifth, the five macros it names (positions, FM, cutoff, drive), of which these are three; estimated: the depths. Macro 1 (Vowel) walks the table; Macro 2 (FM) deepens the bend; Macro 3 (Cutoff) opens the filter.

name: Glide Boom
description: After Attack Magazine's saturated boom bass: a sine falling into each note from above, gliding 300 ms between overlapping notes, with a drive kept off its lowest octave and the highs lifted. From the page: the sine with no detune or random phase, the pitch envelope, the 300 ms glide, the drive above the sub and the high boost; estimated: the dive (+12 over 70 ms), the crossover (a high-pass on the drive's side near 120 Hz). Macro 1 (Grit) drives the upper band; Macro 2 (Glide) lengthens the slide; Macro 3 (Punch) deepens the dive.

name: Jump FM Bass
description: After Attack Magazine's gritty drum and bass bass: a deep sine bent by a modulator two octaves up, the bend rising with an envelope, through a low-pass shut down and opened by another, then a heavy waveshaper. From the page: the +24 modulator, the carrier's own FM at 0, the envelope on the depth, the legato glide, the low cutoff, the shaper, the small reverb, the cut at 250 Hz and lift at 2.5 kHz; estimated: the times (40 ms attack, 300 ms decay). Macro 1 (Ratio) moves the modulator's tuning as the page's XY pad does, through inharmonic ground to three octaves; Macro 2 (FM) deepens the bend; Macro 3 (Drive) pushes the shaper.

name: Liquid Hoover Bass
description: After Alex Blanco's liquid hoover bass for Attack Magazine: a pulse and a saw with their width moved by an LFO in half notes, a sub, each note bending up into pitch from below by its envelope, through a boosted high-pass and a low-pass, chorus making the classic hoover. From the page: the pulse width (46) and its LFO depth (half), the sub, the pitch envelope, the envelopes' shapes, the high-pass, the chorus on for the hoover; estimated: the times in milliseconds and the bend (a whole tone). Macro 1 (Hoover) turns the clean sub version into the full hoover: the chorus in, the bend deeper and the filter open.

name: Mellow Reese
description: After Tim Cant's reese for a synth blog: two oscillators at the middle of a sine-to-square table, three tenths of a semitone either side, mono through a low-pass near 650 Hz, then an overdrive and a notch that moves with the notes. From the page: the table's middle, the +-0.3 semitones (+-0.15 for the mellow one), the 650 Hz and 14 % resonance, the drive, the notch following the notes; estimated: the drive's amount, the notch's place (two octaves over the note). Macro 1 (Beat) widens the tunings to the page's fuller +-0.3; Macro 2 (Cutoff) opens the filter; Macro 3 (Drive) pushes the overdrive.

name: Melodic Techno Bass
description: After Nate Edwards's melodic techno patches for Attack Magazine: a saw and a second an octave up detuned at half its level, with feedback, through a ladder shut and opened by an envelope with a slow-ish attack, then a half-wet chorus. From the page: the octave, the half level, the detune under a third of a notch, the cutoff at zero with the envelope's depth near 4 o'clock and a little emphasis, the envelopes' shapes, the 50/50 chorus, mono; estimated: the times. Macro 1 (Bite) deepens the envelope; Macro 2 (Attack) slows its attack for a wah; Macro 3 (Drive) drives the ladder.

name: Mirror Neuro Bass
description: After Computer Music's neurofunk bass on MusicRadar: one table with a square sub at full level, a two-bar LFO shaped like a shot (a jump, then a fall) sweeping its position and ducking the sub, and a mirror warp that swells in over each note, gliding a quarter second. From the page: the mono glide of 250 ms, the table near 42 of 256, the sub at 100 %, the LFO's 0.55 to the position and -0.4 to the sub, its two-bar restarted cycle, the warp's full swell over 1.7 s; estimated: the drawn shape, the drive. Macro 1 (Tear) starts the mirror further in; Macro 2 (Motion) deepens the sweep; Macro 3 (Drive) pushes the shaper.

name: Morphing FX Bass
description: After Computer Music's walkthrough of a synth's own effects on a bass (MusicRadar): a saw stack through a morphing low-to-high filter near 300 Hz, swept by a bar-long LFO, a down-sampler whose drive the LFO turns the other way, velocity raising resonance and drive, and one macro over every effect's mix. From the page: the cutoff, half resonance, the 30 % morph, the LFO's +10 and -20, the down-sampler at half, velocity's +40 and +20, Macro 1 on every mix; estimated: the source. Macro 1 (FX) brings in all the effects together; Macro 2 (Morph) turns the filter from low toward high.

name: Night Drive Bass
description: After Reverb Machine's synthwave breakdown of a night-drive soundtrack: a saw and a square nine cents apart in a mono five-voice stack barely detuned, through a low-pass near 171 Hz that its envelope throws open and lets fall over half a second, driven, with a lift near 420 Hz. From the page: the stack, the 9 cents (here either side of the note), the cutoff, the envelope's 3.4 and 490 ms decay with no sustain, the amp's 660 ms decay, 0.3 sustain and 660 ms release, the drive and the 420 Hz lift; estimated: the envelope depth in octaves. Macro 1 (Bright) deepens the envelope; Macro 2 (Drive) pushes the drive; Macro 3 (Detune) spreads the stack.

name: Notched Growl
description: After BassGorilla's growl bass walkthrough: two bent tables moved by one drawn LFO in half notes, through a low notch and a vowel filter, then chorus, a diode-like drive, flanger and phaser. From the page: the bend amounts (6 % and 47 %), the second table at 39 %, the LFO's depths on the bends and positions (0.41, 0.27, 0.19, 0.38), the notch at 141 Hz, the vowel filter near 363 Hz, the 1/2 rate; estimated: the vowel's mix (60 % for the page's 40 %), the tables (ours: the basic shapes and the vowels), the drawn shape, the effects' amounts. Macro 1 (Growl) deepens every LFO route at once; Macro 2 (Vowel) moves the vowel; Macro 3 (Drive) pushes the shaper.

name: Octave Saw Bass
description: After Reverb Machine's breakdown of a famous synthwave night-call track: two saws an octave apart, mono, through a resonant low-pass near 727 Hz that decays over 2.5 s, a 5.29 Hz vibrato fading in on the pitch and the cutoff. From the page: the octave, the cutoff, the envelope's 1.7 and its 2.5 s decay, the resonance 6, the LFO's rate on pitch and cutoff with a slow fade; estimated: the depths, the fade's 600 ms. Macro 1 (Vibrato) deepens the vibrato; Macro 2 (Cutoff) opens the filter; Macro 3 (Glide) adds glide.

name: Organ House Bass
description: After Future Music's organ bass on MusicRadar: a triangle-saw blend at the lowest octave under a square three octaves up and a triangle between them, a filter plucked shut, then chorus and a hall. From the page: the octaves (32', 4' and 8'), the levels (a half and a quarter), the filter envelope's three-quarter depth with no sustain, the amp's long decay to half; estimated: the times. Macro 1 (Fifth) tunes the middle triangle up a fifth, as the page suggests; Macro 2 (Pluck) deepens the filter envelope; Macro 3 (Space) widens the hall.

name: Phased Techno Bass
description: After Nate Edwards's phased techno bass for Attack Magazine: one saw, legato, thickened by feedback (here a drive), the filter wide open but pulled back, a four-bar LFO turning it, through a phaser and a plate. From the page: the saw, the legato, the short decay, the feedback under half, the 4/1 synced LFO on the cutoff, the phaser then plate; estimated: the depths and the phaser's settings. Macro 1 (Howl) drives the filter as the page's feedback past half does; Macro 2 (Phase) deepens the phaser; Macro 3 (Plate) wets the reverb.

name: Reese Bass
description: Two saws a few cents apart, beating, through a ladder that barely opens.

name: Riddim Clip Bass
description: After Preset Drive's riddim walkthrough: a saw an octave down in a two-voice stack with a digital table over it, a resonant low-pass snapped open by its envelope, a sine sub, a pitch blip and a hard clip. From the page: the octave, the two voices, the cutoff near 35 % with 40 % resonance, the envelope's 300 ms decay, the amp's 400 ms and 60 %, the blip from +12 over about 30 ms, the clip; estimated: our tables for the page's. Macro 1 (Cutoff) opens it; Macro 2 (Clip) drives the clipper; Macro 3 (Squash) deepens the upward compression.

name: Robot FM Bass
description: After BassGorilla's robotic dubstep bass: a silent sine bends a second oscillator four octaves up, the FM depth drawn by an LFO in half notes, a second LFO in eighths chopping its level, through a resonant high-pass, then chorus, a down-sampler and a phaser. From the page: the octave, the 20 % FM, the 1/2 and 1/8 rates, the high-pass at 41 Hz with 47 % resonance, the down-sampler at 67 % mix; estimated: the drawn shapes, the depths. Macro 1 (Metal) deepens the FM; Macro 2 (Crush) brings up the down-sampler; Macro 3 (Chop) the level LFO.

name: Roller Bass
description: After Nate Edwards's rollers bassline for Attack Magazine: a clean triangle-saw sub through its own 100 Hz low-pass and a dirty layer of a squashed table and a square through a driven 12 dB low-pass near 400 Hz that a slow LFO rolls, then saturation and a phaser. From the page: both layers, the sub's 100 Hz and 40 % resonance, the dirty filter's 400 Hz, 20 % resonance and drive, the LFO's depth, its rate from 0.1 to 4.5 Hz, the reverb near a third; estimated: our tables, the balance. Macro 1 (Roll), the page's one knob, takes the LFO from a slow drift to fast rolls while opening the cutoff and the drive; Macro 2 (Space) widens the reverb.

name: Rolling Reese
description: After Jon Musgrave and Si Truss's classic reese on MusicRadar: two saws a cent apart past half a semitone, started in phase, each a pair of voices a little spread, through a 24 dB low-pass near 4 kHz that a short envelope nudges, with a little noise, gliding legato. From the page: the saws, the reset, the fine tunes of +-61 cents (where the beating meets the tempo), the two voices with 65 % spread and 50 % detune, the 4 kHz cutoff, the envelope's 15 %; estimated: the glide (80 ms), the noise. Macro 1 (Beat) slows the beating by narrowing the tunings; Macro 2 (Cutoff) closes the filter; Macro 3 (Grit) drives it.

name: Rubber Pulse
description: A narrowing pulse through the OTA cascade.

name: Saw-Up Wobble
description: After Computer Music's dubstep wobble on MusicRadar: one square through a low-pass whose cutoff a rising saw LFO in eighths, restarted at each note, throws open, then a fuzz. From the page: the square, the saw-up shape restarted on the gate, the depth about half the range, the low resonance; estimated: the cutoff (about 120 Hz), the fuzz. Macro 1 (Rate) speeds the wobble from eighths to sixteenths; Macro 2 (Grit) sweeps a synced edge in; Macro 3 (Fuzz) drives the shaper.

name: Scream Acid
description: Titan 303's ramp through its own diode ladder, a hard note opening it further.

name: Shy Sub
description: Shy One's square and a sub under it, through its own low-pass, short and round.

name: Squelch Hybrid Bass
description: After BassGorilla's hybrid trap and dubstep bass: two bent tables swept a bar long by a drawn LFO, under a high-pass at 44 Hz, then a diode-like drive, a flanger, a phaser and a low bell boost near 113 Hz. From the page: the LFO's 0.64 to both positions, the bar-long rate, the 8 % bend, the high-pass and its 42 % resonance, the drive's 37 %, the +9.4 dB bell; estimated: the tables and the drawn curve. Macro 1 (Squelch) bends both tables further; Macro 2 (Swirl) brings up the flanger and phaser; Macro 3 (Drive) pushes the shaper.

name: Squish FM Wub
description: After EDMProd's FM dubstep bass: an FM table three octaves down bent by a sine an octave above it, both starting in phase, a drawn LFO in quarters opening a resonant high-pass and the FM, and a square sub on its own filter. From the page: the octaves, the phase reset, the 1/4 rate, the 55 % resonance and 5.6 dB of drive; estimated: the FM depths, the cutoff. Macro 1 (FM) deepens the bend; Macro 2 (Peak) raises the high-pass's resonance; Macro 3 (Rate) speeds the LFO up to twice.

name: Stereo Destructor
description: A good first test of Vitallium in Linux Reaper

name: Sub Thump
description: A triangle and a sub square, short and round.

name: Swelling FM Growl
description: After Future Music's FM growl on MusicRadar: a sine bent by a soft square at twice its pitch, the bend swelling in through each note, an LFO in eighths working it, eight voices detuned and spread, saturated, with noise for fizz and a sub of its own. From the page: the ratio of 2, the slow attack on the FM, the eight voices, the saturation, the noise; estimated: the 300 ms swell, the depths, the high-pass. Macro 1 (Growl) deepens the FM; Macro 2 (Fizz) brings up the noise; Macro 3 (Drive) saturates harder.

name: Swept Unison Reese
description: After Connor Edney's reese tutorial for RouteNote: one saw in six voices, mono and gliding, through a resonant, driven low-pass that a triangle LFO in half notes sweeps across the upper half of its range, its lows notched, then compression and width. From the page: the six voices, the half-note triangle sweeping from 55 % to 95 % of the cutoff, the 75 % resonance and full drive, the glide at half, the two-octave bend; estimated: the detune, the cutoff in hertz. Macro 1 (Sweep) deepens the LFO; Macro 2 (Detune) widens the stack; Macro 3 (Drop) takes the saws down an octave.

name: Tearing Reese
description: After Future Music's tearing neurofunk reese on MusicRadar: a saw whose table runs free on a slow LFO, a sine beating its level (AM) more as each note goes on, noise feeding the fizz, through a notch the LFO sweeps, then drive and compression. From the page: the mono legato glide, the free-running LFO on the table, the AM from a sine raised by a slow-attack envelope, the noise and the sub, the notch, the reverb, compression and distortion; estimated: every number (the LFO near 0.4 Hz, the notch near 1 kHz). Macro 1 (Tear) deepens the AM; Macro 2 (Notch) moves the notch; Macro 3 (Drive) pushes the shaper.

name: Tearout Bass
description: After Preset Drive's tearout bass: a buzzing table an octave down bent by a second, a falling saw LFO in eighths tearing through the first and a square in sixteenths through the second, a notch swept in quarters, then a fold, drive and compression. From the page: the positions (60 % and 40 %), the octave, the FM, the LFOs' shapes, rates and depths (0.5, 0.4), the notch in the middle, the fold's 60 %; estimated: our tables. Macro 1 (Tear) deepens the FM and the LFOs; Macro 2 (Notch) moves the notch; Macro 3 (Fold) folds harder.

name: Techno FM Bass
description: After Audiotent's techno FM bass: a table two octaves down bent by a silent sine an octave down, a bright noise through a 12 dB low-pass beside it, the LFO on the FM, soft-clipped past half. From the page: the octaves, the modulator's silence, the noise through its own low-pass, the LFO on the FM, the clip past half, several settings on one macro; estimated: our table, the depths. Macro 1 (Grind), the page's one knob, deepens the FM and the clip together; Macro 2 (Noise) brings the noise up.

name: Throb Sub
description: After Computer Music's throbbing reese sub on MusicRadar: two sines half a semitone apart either side of the note, beating, over a triangle an octave down, mono through a low-pass that follows the keys fully. From the page: the sines at -50 and +50 cents, the triangle at full level, the 24 dB low-pass near 30 % with full key tracking, the soft attack and release; estimated: the times. Macro 1 (Throb) slows the beating by bringing the sines together; Macro 2 (Body) brings the triangle up.

name: Triplet Pump Bass
description: After Harry Jackson's synthwave bass for Syntorial: a saw and a square an octave down, each three voices lightly detuned, a sine under them, through a resonant analog low-pass and a second gentler one, a falling LFO in eighth-note triplets pumping both, then a soft clip and a chorus. From the page: the octaves, cents (-11 and +9), the three voices at 15 % and 18 %, the resonances (48 % and 31 %), the 1/8T ramp down restarted at each note on both cutoffs, the clip's 6 dB at 24 %, the chorus; estimated: the cutoffs in hertz. Macro 1 (Pump) deepens the LFO; Macro 2 (Cutoff) opens both filters.

name: Triplet Wobble
description: After Roland Schmidt's LFO wobble bass for MusicRadar: a phase-resonant wave plucked by a snappy envelope, a pulse a nineteenth up under it, through a gentle low-pass that a triangle LFO in eighth-note triplets wobbles after a short delay, then a bright drive. From the page: the envelope to the wave (0.62) and to the cutoff, its zero attack and sustain, the +19 semitones at a quarter's level, the 1/8T triangle and its delay, the depth 0.4; estimated: our phase-resonance table for the original's phase distortion, the times. Macro 1 (Wobble) deepens the LFO; Macro 2 (Pluck) deepens the envelope; Macro 3 (Drive) pushes the shaper.

name: Wobble Bass
description: A saw and a sub, the ladder opened and shut by an LFO in eighths.

name: Yoi Bass
description: After Preset Drive's yoi bass: a vowel table an octave down in a two-voice stack, a resonant low-pass and the table both moved by a sine LFO in eighths so each note says yoi, a sine sub and a valve-like drive. From the page: the table near 30 %, the octave, the two voices, the cutoff near 25 % with half resonance, the 1/8 sine on the cutoff and on the position (20 to 30 %), the drive's 40 %, a touch of reverb; estimated: the depths. Macro 1 (Vowel) moves the table; Macro 2 (Rate) speeds the LFO; Macro 3 (Drive) pushes the shaper.

name: Chime Pairs
description: After Martin Russ's practical FM series in Sound On Sound (1988): a chime from carrier and modulator pairs at 1:3 and 2:4, the modulators decaying as the carriers ring, the strike following velocity. From the page: the ratios and their envelopes' shape, the velocity on the modulators; estimated: our depths and times, the third pair (4:8) folded into the second. Macro 1 (Strike) deepens the bends; Macro 2 (Organ) holds the modulators up so a held chord settles into an organ, as the page's variant does.

name: Crystal Glass
description: After the glass and crystal tone an FM cookbook points toward: its bell recipe at a ratio of 3.5, the modulator decaying fast, a long reverb. From the page: the bell recipe; estimated: the ratio and every number. Macro 1 (Glint) deepens the strike; Macro 2 (Shimmer) brings in a shimmering reverb.

name: Inharmonic Bell
description: After an FM synthesis cookbook, its inharmonic bell: a sine bent by a modulator at a ratio of 4.4, the bend dying sooner than the tone, a long decay and release with no sustain. From the page: the non-integer ratio past 4, the shorter modulator decay, the releases past 2 s; estimated: the depths. Macro 1 (Metal) deepens the bend; Macro 2 (Ratio) moves the ratio off toward a clang; Macro 3 (Space) widens the reverb.

name: Silver Bell
description: After Max Rewak's silver bell for the Splice blog: a sine two voices slightly apart, bent 22 % by a silent harmonic table three octaves, two semitones and 18 cents up, an envelope adding 28 % at each strike, a sine sub under it, a metal tick from the noise, flanged, chorused and reverberant. From the page: the FM's 22 % and +28 %, the modulator's tuning, the sub, the tick; estimated: the amp (0/3 s/0/3 s) and the effects' amounts. Macro 1 (Strike) deepens the strike and the tick; Macro 2 (Shimmer) brings up the flanger and chorus.

name: Struck Can
description: After Alex Blanco's eighties tuned percussion for Attack Magazine: a burst of noise striking a resonator, here a comb filter tuned by the keys, ringing like a punched can, a second ring an octave up beside it, a little stereo spread. From the page: the noise burst's 0/400/0/0, the resonator struck with its dry sound suppressed, the second layer an octave up with a stereo detune; estimated: the comb's feedback and our units. Macro 1 (Material) lengthens the ring; Macro 2 (Bright) brightens the strike.

name: Techno FM Bell
description: After Nate Edwards's melodic techno patches for Attack Magazine, its bell: the FM table through a resonant low-pass into a high-pass, an envelope walking the table, a random step LFO over ten seconds moving it too, half-wet reverb, panned wide. From the page: the filters, the amp's decay and release, the envelope on the table, the random LFO's 40, the reverb near half; estimated: our units, and the table's place, a quarter in where the note leads (the page's two thirds puts our table's fifth harmonic over it, a third above the key). Macro 1 (Shimmer) deepens the envelope and the random LFO; Macro 2 (Space) the reverb.

name: Vibrato FM Bell
description: After Syntorial's recipe for a mono FM bell: a sine bent 15 % by a silent triangle thirty-four semitones up, mono, high-passed, a fast triangle vibrato in sixteenths of 42 cents, a slow chorus and a medium reverb. From the page: all of it; estimated: the high-pass in hertz. Macro 1 (Tine) deepens the bend; Macro 2 (Vibrato) deepens the vibrato; Macro 3 (Space) the reverb.

name: Wood Knock Mallet
description: After Attack Magazine's sine percussion lead: a sine whose pitch knocks down from two octaves up in a few milliseconds at each note (deeper sounds metallic, shallower woody), a little sustain and release, a dubby echo with a dotted-quarter tap, a light reverb. From the page: the knock on the pitch with no sustain, the echo; estimated: the knock's 24 semitones and 20 ms, our table (the harmonic build near its start, a sine with a little of its second harmonic). Macro 1 (Metal) deepens the knock from wood toward metal; Macro 2 (Echo) brings up the delay.

name: Cinematic Swell Brass
description: After Syntorial's recipe for a slow, cinematic synth brass: a saw two voices five cents apart spread full, squeezed by its warp at 76 %, through an analog low-pass near 331 Hz with some resonance and drive that a slow envelope opens by a third, a perlin-like random LFO in quarters drifting the tuning, a reverb, and the wheel opening the filter, taming the resonance and widening the reverb. From the page: all of it, the amp's 120 ms and 629 ms, the envelope's 709/1080/82 %/2110, the reverb's 39 % at 2.3 s; estimated: our units. Macro 1 (Swell), the page's wheel, does what it does; Macro 2 (Drift) deepens the tuning's drift.

name: Rasp Brass
description: After Gordon Reid's brass on a famous monosynth in Sound On Sound's Synth Secrets: one saw through a ladder shut at the bottom with a little resonance, its envelope opening it slowly (600 ms) and falling over 800 ms to half, the keys followed fully, a 100 ms attack, and a low triangle beating the cutoff at audio rate (three octaves under the saw, its key tracking off) for the growl the wheel brings in. From the page: the saw at 4', the amp's 100 ms with full sustain and no release, the envelope's 600/800/half, the 6.5 contour, the full key tracking, the low triangle on the cutoff by the wheel; estimated: our units. Macro 1 (Rasp), the page's wheel, brings the growl in; Macro 2 (Bite) speeds the filter's opening.

name: Retro Poly Brass
description: A synthwave poly brass on the advice Attack Magazine's lush keys piece gives for true brass: the filter's attack a little slower than the amp's, so each chord swells brighter just after it starts; two detuned saws through a warm low-pass, a chorus and a plate. Designed on the instrument. Macro 1 (Swell) slows the filter's attack further and deepens it; Macro 2 (Bright) opens the filter.

name: Trailer Braam
description: After a DAW maker's blog on high-impact sounds for trailers: a long, loud, low braam of saws an octave below and above the note, the filter swelling open, driven, the whole falling slowly in pitch through its tail, into a big reverb. From the page: the octave layers, the distortion, the slow pitch-down, the shared reverb; estimated: every number (a fall of a semitone and a half over three seconds). Macro 1 (Weight) brings the octave layers and the drive up; Macro 2 (Fall) deepens the pitch-down.

name: Big Room Saw Chords
description: After Maxim Hetman's supersaw article for Monosounds, its big-room variant: two seven-voice saws at a moderate detune with an octave-up layer, a long reverb and a heavy pump. From the page: the voices, the 0.12 detune, the +12 layer, the long reverb and heavy sidechain; estimated: the pump's shape (Pulsar in quarters), the levels. Macro 1 (Pump) deepens the duck; Macro 2 (Size) widens the detune and the reverb; Macro 3 (Top) brings the octave layer up.

name: Chillwave Chords
description: After Syntorial's recipe for soft chillwave chords: a saw two voices three cents apart started in phase, a 20 ms attack and a decay to 70 %, a resonant low-pass at a third plucked by a short envelope that releases very slowly, the wheel opening it, into a big reverb. From the page: all of it, the wheel's 30 % on the cutoff; estimated: the cutoff in hertz. Macro 1 (Open), the page's wheel, opens the filter; Macro 2 (Space) widens the reverb.

name: Clean Supersaw Chords
description: After Matt Hardy's supersaw piece for FaderPro: a seven-voice saw at a moderate detune over a three-voice saw an octave down, the lower one trimmed by its own low-pass and both high-passed, a slow attack opening the filter too, into a short trimmed reverb. From the page: the voices and detunes (20 %, 7 %), the octave, the routing, the attack routed to the cutoff, the reverb near 500 ms at 30 to 40 %; estimated: the attack (40 ms), the cutoffs. Macro 1 (Detune) widens the stack from 5 % toward 40 %; Macro 2 (Low) brings the octave down up.

name: Deep Ninth Stab
description: A deep house minor ninth under one finger, after the voicing ModeAudio gives (root, minor third, fifth, seventh and ninth): a minor-chord stack on the first oscillator, the seventh and ninth on the others, through a warm low-pass plucked open, a slow chorus and a room. From the page: the intervals; designed: the rest. Macro 1 (Cutoff) opens the filter; Macro 2 (Decay) lets the chord ring; Macro 3 (Space) widens the room.

name: Dub Techno Chord
description: After Adam Douglas's dub techno chords for Attack Magazine: a saw and a square with a little noise, high-passed with a slow LFO on it, a soft attack, through a phaser and a plate, a mid cut near 600 Hz, then a long dotted echo with heavy feedback. From the page: the oscillators and noise, the high-pass's cutoff and resonance, the LFO on it, the amp's shape, the phaser's settings, the plate, the 600 Hz cut and the band from 100 Hz to 4.5 kHz, the dotted-eighth echo; estimated: our units. Macro 1 (Dub), the dub space, raises the echo's feedback and mix together; Macro 2 (Phase) deepens the phaser; Macro 3 (Cutoff) closes the low-pass.

name: Flutter Swell Chords
description: After Production Music Live's future bass synth for beginners: a five-voice saw through a closed filter that a slow envelope (about 685 ms) swells open while a sixteenth-note LFO flutters it, a little reverb. From the page: the voices, the closed cutoff, the envelope's attack and its 30 % reach, the 1/16 LFO at half, the 10 % reverb; estimated: the detune. Macro 1 (Flutter) deepens the flutter; Macro 2 (Swell) slows the swell; Macro 3 (Rate) doubles the flutter toward thirty-seconds.

name: Future Rave Saws
description: After Maxim Hetman's supersaw article for Monosounds, its future-rave variant: five voices at a light detune through a low-pass resting near 600 Hz and swept between 400 and 900, with light upward compression. From the page: the voices, the 0.09 detune, the cutoff's home and sweep, the light compression, the advice against wide detunes; estimated: our detune. Macro 1 (Sweep) sweeps the cutoff from 400 Hz up past 900 and on; Macro 2 (Drop) brings in an octave-up layer as the page's drop layer does.

name: Future Wobble Chords
description: After Maxim Hetman's future bass chords for Monosounds: a seven-voice saw, a saw an octave up at 60 % and a sine an octave down, through a 24 dB low-pass that a sine in half notes wobbles from about 800 Hz toward 8 kHz, a drawn dip-and-ramp in quarters ducking the volume as a sidechain would, squashed, into a big hall. From the page: the voices, detunes (0.15, 0.18), levels, the 800 Hz cutoff and its sweep, both LFOs' rates and the volume's 60 to 80 %, the compression near 60 % mix, the 25 % hall; estimated: our detunes in semitones. Macro 1 (Wobble) deepens the filter LFO; Macro 2 (Rate) doubles both LFOs; Macro 3 (Pump) deepens the duck.

name: Gated Future Pluck
description: After Computer Music's futuristic gated synth pluck on MusicRadar: a three-voice saw spread wide, a steep high-pass halfway following the keys into a steep low-pass that a saw LFO in eighths chops shut and lifts the resonance of, chorused, saturated and limited into a bright hall. From the page: the stack (3, detune near 43), the filters' order and slopes, the saw LFO's 1/8 and its -60 on the cutoff and +10 on the resonance, the chorus's 25 %, the hall; estimated: the cutoffs in hertz. Macro 1 (Gate), the page's wheel, deepens the chop; Macro 2 (Darken) closes the low-pass; Macro 3 (Space) widens the hall.

name: Old School House Stab
description: After Attack Magazine's old-school house chords: three oscillators at the root, a minor third and a fifth, so one key plays the chord, each a pair of voices spread five cents, through a 24 dB low-pass shut and plucked open by a fast envelope, a reverb and a chorus. From the page: the intervals, the full levels and tables, the two voices and their spread, the closed cutoff and the envelope near 2 o'clock; estimated: the decay (300 ms). Macro 1 (Color) moves the chord to the darker 0, 5, 8 the page offers; Macro 2 (Pluck) deepens the envelope; Macro 3 (Space) widens the reverb.

name: Pulsing Table Chords
description: After Attack Magazine's piece on modulating a synth's own effects into pulsing plucks: two crushed tables in small stacks, a drawn LFO in eighth-note triplets on the cutoff, a half-note LFO walking both tables and a rising ramp pulling both levels down and up again as an internal sidechain, the envelope opening the reverb. From the page: the stacks (4 at 0.10, 3 at 0.16), the LFOs' shapes, rates and the ramp's full depth, the levels near a quarter, the reverb on the envelope; estimated: our tables (bit steps and a fold), the filter. Macro 1 (Pump) deepens the ramp; Macro 2 (Morph) moves the tables; Macro 3 (Space) widens the reverb.

name: Rave Minor Stab
description: After Si Truss's classic rave chord stab for MusicRadar: an organ table held as a minor seventh under one finger, a square an octave and ten cents up with a sub, through a 12 dB low-pass near 150 Hz that a fast envelope throws open, a short release, a touch of crushing and a big reverb. From the page: the minor seventh from one key, the organ table, the square's +12 and +10 cents, the sub, the 150 Hz cutoff, the envelope's 60 % with a little sustain, the crusher; estimated: the decay, the mixes. Macro 1 (Crunch) brings the crusher and the envelope up together; Macro 2 (Space) the reverb.

name: Rhythm Swell Chords
description: After Syntorial's recipe for a melodic-bass chord pluck: an eight-voice saw through a resonant, driven 24 dB low-pass and a gentle high-pass, a triangle in sixteenths fluttering the cutoff, a slow eight-bar swell opening it and a triangle in quarters wobbling the level, a little reverb. From the page: the voices, the 7 % detune, the cutoffs near 129 and 272 Hz with 22 % and 6 % resonance, the 12 % drive, the three LFOs and their depths (36 %, 88 %, 60 %), the 8 % reverb; estimated: our units. Macro 1 (Swell), the page's build-up opener, opens the cutoff as the slow LFO would; Macro 2 (Flutter) deepens the sixteenths; Macro 3 (Wobble) the level.

name: Square Layer Chords
description: After Preset Drive's future bass chords: a seven-voice saw over a square stack an octave up at a third of its level, a 24 dB low-pass at two thirds with its envelope opening it a little, a quick attack and a 300 ms release, squashed hard, a slow chorus and a hall. From the page: the voices and detunes (0.22, 0.2), the square's level, the cutoff, the 20 % envelope, the amp's 10 ms, 85 % and 300 ms, the hall's 25 %; estimated: the cutoff in hertz. Macro 1 (Square) brings the square layer up; Macro 2 (Squash) deepens the upward compression; Macro 3 (Cutoff) opens the filter.

name: Techno Square Stab
description: After Attack Magazine's techno synth stabs: a square through a shut filter its envelope plucks open, a short decay to nothing, a soft clip, a little overdrive and saturation, a very short room before them and a subtle ping-pong. From the page: the square, the closed cutoff and the envelope near 3 o'clock, the amp's 0/66/0/29, the envelope's 5/48/9/24, the drives, the reverb's 3 ms, the ping-pong; estimated: those times in ms. Macro 1 (Womp), the page's last-note move, slows the envelope's attack and shortens its decay; Macro 2 (Drive) pushes the saturation; Macro 3 (Echo) the ping-pong.

name: Ambient Stack Drone
description: After Future Music's ambient drone on MusicRadar: three saws at the note and one and two octaves down, the middle one detuned and drifting on an eight-bar LFO, panned apart through a low cutoff, a slowly turning harmonic table under them. From the page: the octaves, the detune near 25 and its eight-bar LFO, the low cutoff with a little LFO, the slow table (0.01 Hz); estimated: our units. Macro 1 (Depth) brings the lowest layer up and opens the cutoff; Macro 2 (Motion) speeds the table's turn.

name: Pulsing Saw Drone
description: After Alex Blanco's drones for Attack Magazine: a saw an octave up through a nearly open low-pass with a little emphasis, amp and filter envelopes pumping as notes repeat, velocity driving the level fully, notches at 150, 300, 600 and 1200 Hz, a huge plate. From the page: the octave, the cutoff (108 of 120) and emphasis, the envelopes (49/75/-/29 and 68/49/0), velocity, the four notches, the plate; estimated: our units. Macro 1 (Pump) deepens the filter envelope and slows its attack; Macro 2 (Plate) widens the plate.

name: Ring Mod Drone
description: A metallic sci-fi drone: a saw ring-modulated by a sine a minor ninth away, its table and the ring's depth wandering on slow LFOs, a resonant band-pass drifting through it, a flanger and a long reverb. Designed on the instrument. Macro 1 (Ring) deepens the ring; Macro 2 (Sweep) widens the band-pass's drift; Macro 3 (Flange) the flanger.

name: Rumble Drone
description: After Computer Music's rumbling techno kicks on MusicRadar: a sine and some noise sent through heavy distortion, then a hall with its lows lifted, a swung echo and a steep low-pass near 800 Hz, the dark rumble that sits under a techno kick, here held as a drone. From the page: the chain (drive, hall, echo, steep low-pass at 800 Hz); estimated: every amount. Macro 1 (Rumble) wets the hall and opens the low-pass; Macro 2 (Grit) drives harder.

name: Tension Drone
description: A cinematic tension bed: a low saw stack with a fifth and a tritone slowly fading in and out of it on smooth random LFOs, through a dark ladder that breathes, a high whistle of noise, a long hall. Designed on the instrument. Macro 1 (Tension) brings the tritone forward; Macro 2 (Air) the whistle; Macro 3 (Space) the hall.

name: Additive Riser
description: After Aykan Esen's risers for Attack Magazine: a harmonic table whose position an LFO lifts, noise rising from three octaves under to three over, a resonant low-pass near 5.5 kHz, a feeding echo, a slow flanger, a chorus and a big reverb, louder at the end. From the page: the noise's -36 to +36, the resonance near 0.7, the cutoff, the echo's eighths and feedback, the flanger, chorus and the reverb's 44 %; estimated: our table for the additive engine, the times. Macro 1 (Rise) deepens the climb; Macro 2 (Space) widens the reverb.

name: Bomb Impact
description: After Attack Magazine's transition FX masterclass, its bomb: a long, deep kick (a sine falling in pitch, a burst of noise) into a concert hall of about ten seconds with almost no pre-delay, its lows cut at 410 Hz and a big high shelf. From the page: the long kick, the hall's 10 s and 6 ms, the reverb's low cut at 410 Hz and high cut near 15 kHz, the +8.5 dB shelf from 670 Hz; estimated: the kick. Macro 1 (Size) lengthens the hall; Macro 2 (Drop) deepens the pitch fall.

name: Bubble Computer
description: A sample-and-hold computer: a random step LFO in sixteenths jumping the pitch and a resonant band-pass, the bubbling of Computer Music's classic effects list. From the page: the idea (random steps on the pitch); designed: every number. Macro 1 (Range) widens the jumps; Macro 2 (Rate) speeds them; Macro 3 (Echo) the delay.

name: Downer Sweep
description: After Computer Music's basic synth downer on MusicRadar: two sines panned hard left and right and a hundred cents apart, a long high note falling two octaves, a slight distortion, a room and a sixteenth-note ping-pong. From the page: the sines, the panning, the -100 and +100 cents, the two-octave fall, the effects; estimated: the fall's curve and time. Macro 1 (Fall) deepens the fall; Macro 2 (Echo) brings up the ping-pong.

name: Formant Sweep
description: After Attack Magazine's transition FX masterclass, its formant sweep: a harsh digital table at its middle held low, through a formant filter an envelope walks from end to end over the note, a dense reverb at a quarter. From the page: the held low note, the table's middle, the formant swept by an envelope with no attack and a full decay, the reverb's 25 %; estimated: our table and the times. Macro 1 (Vowel) shifts the vowels the sweep passes through; Macro 2 (Space) widens the reverb.

name: Laser Zap
description: A self-oscillating filter zapped down by a fast envelope, as Computer Music's classic effects list describes the zap: the resonance at the top, the cutoff falling fast, a little noise for the edge, an echo. From the page: the idea (maximum resonance, the cutoff dropped by an envelope, reverb); designed: every number. Macro 1 (Length) slows the fall; Macro 2 (Echo) brings the delay up.

name: Manic Pitch Rise
description: After Attack Magazine's transition FX masterclass, its manic pitch rise: two oscillators an octave apart, their pitch shaken by a sixteenth-note LFO whose depth grows from small to big as the note holds, into a half-wet hall with a lifted top. From the page: the octave, the LFO on the pitch in sixteenths, its depth growing, the hall near 50 % and the shelf near 5 kHz; estimated: our units. Macro 1 (Tension) speeds and deepens the shake; Macro 2 (Space) widens the hall.

name: Noise Riser
description: Noise through a resonant band-pass that sweeps up as the note is held.

name: Phase Rise
description: A resonance climbing through a falling saw as the note is held.

name: Sci-Fi Riser
description: After Computer Music's ten classic synth effects on MusicRadar, its sci-fi riser: a square whose pitch a square LFO at 38 Hz throws a full octave up and down, the LFO faded in over some ten seconds, into a reverb. From the page: the square, the 38 Hz square LFO on the pitch at full depth, the 8 to 10 s fade, the reverb; estimated: our depth (an octave each way) and the reverb. Macro 1 (Chaos) speeds the LFO and deepens it; Macro 2 (Space) widens the reverb.

name: Sub Boom
description: After Adam Douglas's booms for Attack Magazine: one sine at the lowest octave, an instant attack and a full decay to nothing, its pitch falling from an envelope at half depth over about a second, saturated, mono, compressed. From the page: the sine at 32', the amp's shape, the envelope's half depth, 1160 decay and 10 sustain, the saturation; estimated: our units. Macro 1 (Drop) deepens the pitch fall; Macro 2 (Grit) drives the saturation.

name: Wind-Up
description: After Attack Magazine's transition FX masterclass, its wind-up: noise through a resonant low-pass a third open that an LFO sweeps fully, the LFO speeding up toward the drop, a light reverb. From the page: the cutoff and resonance near a third, the LFO's full depth, its rate climbing; estimated: the climb (four octaves over the note). Macro 1 (Tension) speeds the LFO further; Macro 2 (Space) widens the reverb.

name: Brass Stab
description: A Sallen-Key that swells open, as analog brass does.

name: Crushed Lo-fi Keys
description: After MusicRadar's three techniques for dusty lo-fi, its down-sampler: soft keys of a triangle and a quiet saw through a 12-bit crusher at a lowered rate, high-passed at 100 Hz and low-passed at 12 kHz as the page suggests. From the page: the bit depths (12, and 8 for its harsher setting), the rate's halving, the EQ; designed: the keys. Macro 1 (Crush) walks from 12 bits to 6 and lowers the rate; Macro 2 (Tone) opens the low-pass.

name: Digital Tine Keys
description: After an FM synthesis cookbook, its digital electric piano: a sine bent by a modulator fourteen times its pitch with a short decay, beside a second sine slightly detuned bending itself about as a 2:1 pair would, decaying in some 500 ms, the tone dying over a few seconds, chorus and phaser. From the page: the ratios, the decays (2 to 4 s and some 500 ms), the detune, the chorus and phaser; estimated: the depths, the self-bend for the 2:1 pair. Macro 1 (Bark) deepens the tine's strike; Macro 2 (Body) the second sine's bend; Macro 3 (Phase) wets the phaser.

name: Drawbar Organ
description: An organ's registration, full on at each key, a little chorus in unison.

name: Dusty Tape Keys
description: After Reverb Machine's lo-fi bedroom-pop breakdown, its first keys, with the master tape the page puts on everything: a saw through a high-pass a third up and a low low-pass that follows the keys halfway, a plucky envelope, no chorus, then a dusty, wobbling tape with hiss and a crushed edge. From the page: the filters (3, 3, 2), the envelope (3, decay 5, no sustain, release 4), the key tracking, the tape; estimated: the crusher and our units. Macro 1 (Dust) brings up the hiss and the crush; Macro 2 (Wow) the tape's wobble, on the pitch too.

name: Eighties Saw Keys
description: After Alex Blanco's versatile eighties synth keys for Attack Magazine: two saws, the second an octave down at three quarters, the voices drifting apart (the page's 41 % detune), noise at 40, through a low-pass at a quarter opened 60 % by its envelope, a decay to nothing, all on tape. From the page: the oscillators, the detune, the noise, the cutoff and envelope (0/60/50/55), the amp's 0/60/0/20, the tape; estimated: our units. Macro 1 (Age) brings the noise up and wobbles the pitch and the tape; Macro 2 (Sustain) holds the notes for chords; Macro 3 (Bright) opens the filter.

name: Hazy Lo-fi Keys
description: After Reverb Machine's lo-fi bedroom-pop breakdown, its second keys: a saw through a high-pass a third up and a low, gently resonant low-pass that the envelope and a free 1.32 Hz LFO move, half the key tracking, a small reverb, all on tape that wows. From the page: the high-pass (3.5), cutoff (1.3), resonance (2), envelope (4), LFO (5 at 1.32 Hz), key tracking (5), the envelope (1/6/2.5/0), the small reverb and the tape; estimated: our units. Macro 1 (Warble) deepens the tape's wow and adds a pitch wobble; Macro 2 (Tone) opens the low-pass.

name: Night Call Keys
description: After Syntorial's recipe for synthwave night-drive keys: a saw two voices eight cents apart spread 60 %, started in phase, with 15 % noise, through a resonant low-pass half open that a 3.7 s envelope closes from bright, a full sustain and a 20 ms release, a slow chorus and a medium reverb. From the page: all of it; estimated: the cutoff in hertz. Macro 1 (Tail) lengthens the filter's fall and deepens it; Macro 2 (Chorus) wets the chorus; Macro 3 (Space) the reverb.

name: Poly Keys
description: A pulse and a saw that open with how hard each note is played.

name: Promise Brass
description: Promise Bloom's two saws apart through its own low-pass, which swells open as brass does.

name: Resonant Ensemble Keys
description: After Attack Magazine's lush keys in the manner of a famous eighties film composer: one saw through a very resonant low-pass its envelope plucks, velocity on both envelopes, an ensemble chorus, a plate and a narrow dip near 680 Hz with a low cut. From the page: the cutoff, resonance and envelope (91, 88, 42 on that synth), the envelopes' shapes, velocity at 83, the chorus's rate, depth and 39 % wet, the plate's 59 % and its decay, the EQ; estimated: our units. Macro 1 (Ping) raises the resonance and the envelope; Macro 2 (Space) widens the plate.

name: Sine Ring Keys
description: After Syntorial's recipe for pure, decaying sine keys: a sine two voices two cents apart, started in phase, a six-second decay and release, velocity on the level, a big reverb. From the page: all of it; designed: a quiet sine two octaves up with a short decay for its music-box variant, which the page's notes suggest. Macro 1 (Ring) lengthens the decay; Macro 2 (Box) brings the music-box octave in; Macro 3 (Space) the reverb.

name: Square Vibrato Keys
description: After Reverb Machine's lo-fi chords breakdown: a square alone, a slow vibrato on it, a high-pass and a low-pass both halfway, a fast attack and decay to a half sustain and release, with a slow auto-pan and more reverb for the pad version. From the page: the square, the vibrato's depth and 0.95 Hz, the filters, the envelope; estimated: our units. Macro 1 (Vibrato) deepens the vibrato; Macro 2 (Pad) slows the attack, widens the pan and the reverb toward the page's pad layer.

name: Tremolo Dream Keys
description: After Reverb Machine's dreamy psychedelic-pop breakdown, its electric piano treatment: a soft tine tone with a tremolo, a chorus, and a cheap tape wobbling on a sine. From the page: the tremolo's rate and shallow depth, the chorus, the cheap tape with its low and high cuts; estimated: the tone (a sine bent a little by a silent sine fourteen times up, as an electric piano is often made, a triangle an octave up beside it) and our units. Macro 1 (Tremolo) deepens the tremolo; Macro 2 (Tine) brings out the tine's bark; Macro 3 (Wow) the tape.

name: Anthem Supersaw Lead
description: After Joe Hanley's giant supersaw trance lead for Syntorial: three saws nine voices deep, the second a little flat and the third a little sharp, detuned until they just start to sound out of tune and spread full width, white noise four octaves up in the same stack, a gentle high-pass, a quick decay to a low sustain, a touch of clipping, a big damped hall and compression. From the page: everything but the numbers; estimated: the detune (a quarter of a semitone), the decay (450 ms to 45 %), the noise level, the mixes. Macro 1 (Size) widens the detune and the hall together; Macro 2 (Air) brings up the noise; Macro 3 (Sustain) holds the notes fuller.

name: Big Room Zap Lead
description: After Syntorial's recipe for a festival big-room lead: a saw four voices nineteen cents apart with a little noise, high-passed thin and bright, each note zapping down three octaves in 10 ms, a full-wet slow chorus and a medium reverb, a vibrato on the wheel. From the page: all of it, the wheel's 25 % on an eighth-note vibrato too; estimated: the high-pass in hertz, and the upward compression the page says it is used with. Macro 1 (Zap) deepens the pitch drop and the noise; Macro 2 (Thin) raises the high-pass; Macro 3 (Space) widens the reverb.

name: Bounce Square Lead
description: After W. A. Production's future house lead: a square five voices lightly detuned over a three-voice square and a saw sub, mono gliding 40 ms, both in pulse-width warp moved by a drawn pluck-shaped envelope in half notes, through a 12 dB low-pass, soft-clipped, then a plate. From the page: the oscillators and voices, the pulse-width warp, the envelope-mode LFO at 1/2, the glide, the filter, the effects; estimated: the depths, which the page shows only in pictures. Macro 1 (Bounce) deepens the pulse movement; Macro 2 (Cutoff) opens the filter; Macro 3 (Space) widens the plate.

name: Chip Square Lead
description: After Syntorial's recipe for a bright eighties synth-pop lead: two half-width pulses an octave apart (40 % and 60 %), four voices nine cents apart, mono, the filter near 85 %, a short release and a little reverb. From the page: all of it; estimated: the cutoff in hertz. Macro 1 (Width) narrows both pulses; Macro 2 (Detune) spreads the stack; Macro 3 (Space) widens the reverb.

name: Chip Unison Lead
description: After BassGorilla's chiptune lead: a pulse-width table near its square, sixteen voices barely detuned, its width swept a bar long, over a sixteen-voice saw, mono gliding 65 ms, chorused and lifted by a multiband compressor, with a reverb and a ping-pong echo after it. From the page: the positions (12 and 2), the voices, the LFO's 82 over a bar, the glide, the chorus's 34 %, the reverb's 28 % at 2.4 s, the echo's 24 % with 51 % feedback; estimated: our detunes. Macro 1 (Chip) deepens the width sweep and lowers the saw for a purer square; Macro 2 (Echo) the delay; Macro 3 (Space) the reverb.

name: Cinematic Swell Lead
description: After Computer Music's classic cinematic lead on MusicRadar: one oscillator whose amp and filter share a slow attack, the low-pass opening wide with it, into a long echo and a seven-second reverb. From the page: the single oscillator, the shared envelope (attack 40, sustain full, release 85 on that synth), the cutoff at 40 and its depth of 90, the delay's 30, the reverb's 7 s; estimated: the times in ms, and a delayed vibrato and an 80 ms glide the page leaves out. Macro 1 (Expression) opens the filter and deepens the vibrato; Macro 2 (Attack) slows the swell; Macro 3 (Space) the reverb.

name: Crunch Pluck Lead
description: After The Producer School's future big-room pluck lead: a sine-kick table four voices wide over a five-voice saw, a 600 ms decay to nothing also closing a 12 dB ladder, each note bent down an octave from a very short envelope, gliding 200 ms, through a sine shaper at about half and a second low-pass after it. From the page: the voices, the detune, the decay, the +12 blip, the glide, the shaper's 55 %, the low-passes; estimated: our tables, the cutoffs. Macro 1 (Crunch) drives the shaper and opens the low-pass after it; Macro 2 (Decay) lets the notes ring.

name: Delayed Vibrato Lead
description: After Max Rewak's lead tips for the Splice blog: a mono saw stack with a small glide, a 7 Hz vibrato coming in after 200 ms, a light down-sampler and a quick compressor. From the page: the glide, the vibrato's rate and delay, the down-sampler, the 3 to 4:1 compression; estimated: the stack and the depths. Macro 1 (Vibrato) deepens the vibrato; Macro 2 (Crush) brings up the down-sampler; Macro 3 (Echo) a quarter-note delay.

name: Echo Bell Lead
description: After Syntorial's recipe for a bell-ish eighties lead: a quiet saw under a triangle an octave up, two voices five cents apart started in phase, mono, a ten-second decay to half, a short pluck of the filter, an eighth-note echo and a reverb. From the page: the levels (20 % and 80 %), the unison, the 0/10000/50 %/20 amp, the cutoff at 70 %, the envelope's 10 % over 700 ms, the echo's 35 % with 10 % feedback, the 20 % reverb; estimated: the cutoff in hertz. Macro 1 (Echo) brings the delay and its feedback up; Macro 2 (Bell) brings the saw down for a purer bell.

name: Fractal Sync Lead
description: After Roland Schmidt's fractal sync tone for MusicRadar: a synced saw whose sync sweeps down at each new note on a quick envelope, legato with glide, an echo and compression. From the page: the 0/50/100/20 amp, the envelope's 0/63/0/20 sweeping the sync and the shape, the legato glide, the delay; estimated: our sync table for the page's fractal mode, the sweep's depth and its 600 ms. Macro 1 (Sweep) deepens the sync sweep; Macro 2 (Sync) moves the sync's resting place higher; Macro 3 (Echo) the delay.

name: Gliding Trance Lead
description: After Syntorial's recipe for a smooth uplifting trance lead: two saws three cents either side of the note, free-running, mono with a 50 ms glide, the filter nearly open, a triangle vibrato in eighths brought in by the wheel, a big reverb. From the page: the cents, the levels, the glide, the 0/100 %/20 ms amp, the cutoff at 90 %, the vibrato's rate and the wheel's 10 %, the 20 % reverb; estimated: a dotted-eighth echo, which the page suggests. Macro 1 (Vibrato) brings the vibrato in as the wheel does; Macro 2 (Echo) the delay; Macro 3 (Space) the reverb.

name: Hard Trance Lead
description: After Syntorial's recipe for a gritty hard-trance lead: a saw and a wide pulse thirty-one semitones up, mono, a six-second decay to nothing, a resonant low-pass, driven hard, a little reverb. From the page: the waves, the +31, the even levels, the 0/6000 ms/0/20 ms amp, the cutoff at 70 % and 40 % resonance, the 68 % drive, the 10 % reverb; estimated: the cutoff in hertz. Macro 1 (Grit) drives harder and raises the resonance; Macro 2 (Cutoff) opens the filter.

name: Hollow Trance Lead
description: After Syntorial's recipe for a bright, hollow trance lead: a square under a saw an octave up (30 % and 70 %), every oscillator two voices nine cents apart, mono, a 10 ms attack, the filter near 85 %, a medium reverb. From the page: all of it; estimated: the cutoff in hertz. Macro 1 (Hollow) crossfades toward the square; Macro 2 (Cutoff) closes the filter; Macro 3 (Space) widens the reverb.

name: Hoover Stab
description: After Computer Music's drum and bass hoover stab on MusicRadar: two wide saw stacks, the first an octave up, over a saw an octave down, each note bending up a fifth and back, a synced sine LFO working the drive and the balance, distorted at half and crushed a little, a short room and a tape-like echo. From the page: the octaves, the wide stacks, the +7 pitch envelope rising and falling, the LFO on the drive's mix and the balance, the half distortion, the crusher, the reverb and the 278 ms echo low in the mix, the two macros it sets up (one for the reverb, one for the filter and release); estimated: the times, the voices (eight at 0.4). Macro 1 (Space) widens the reverb and lengthens its decay; Macro 2 (Tone) closes the filter and lengthens the release.

name: Lo-fi Tape Lead
description: After Adam Douglas's lo-fi synth lead for Attack Magazine: two saws, the second slightly detuned and low, a soft attack and full sustain, a slow pitch wobble bending them slightly flat, a folding drive, heavy tape, a short dark chorus and a high-passed band lifted near 1.45 kHz, into a long, noisy tape echo. From the page: the levels, the cutoff near 65, the envelope's 20, the amp's 40/80/70/60, the wobble's rate near 3, the fold's 5 dB, the high-pass near 350 Hz, the lift at 1.45 kHz, the 315 ms echo with strong feedback; estimated: our units. Macro 1 (Wow) deepens the wobble and the echo's wow; Macro 2 (Echo) brings the tape echo up.

name: Moonbeam Lead
description: Mini Moonbeam's saw and square through the transistor ladder, gliding, its vibrato coming in late.

name: Nasal Square Lead
description: After Syntorial's recipe for a nasal, emotional future-bass square lead: two squares, the second a nineteenth up and five cents flat, two voices nineteen cents apart, mono, a long decay, through a band-pass following the keys and plucked by its envelope, distorted, with an echo and a reverb. From the page: the levels (70 % and 30 %), the interval, the unison, the 0/1900/40 %/350 amp, the band-pass at 45 % with its 15 % resonance and 40 % key tracking, the envelope's 20 %, the 56 % distortion, the echo and reverb; estimated: the band in hertz. Macro 1 (Formant) sweeps the band-pass; Macro 2 (Drive) pushes the distortion; Macro 3 (Echo) the delay.

name: Night Vibrato Lead
description: After Reverb Machine's synthwave breakdown of a night-drive soundtrack: three saws at 0, -13 and +10 cents, a small 4.56 Hz vibrato, driven at half, high-passed at 75 Hz, lifted at 1.8 kHz and low-passed near 6.3 kHz. From the page: all of it; estimated: our turn of its vibrato depth into cents. Macro 1 (Vibrato) deepens the vibrato; Macro 2 (Drive) pushes the drive; Macro 3 (Echo) brings in a dotted-eighth delay.

name: PWM Brass Lead
description: After Syntorial's recipe for a brassy eighties pulse lead: one pulse whose width a triangle in eighths moves deeply, mono, a 90 ms attack and a three-second decay to 30 %, through a resonant low-pass that its own envelope opens a little, a slow chorus and a reverb. From the page: the 50 % pulse, the amp's 90/3050/30 %/450, the cutoff at 40 % with 45 % resonance, the envelope's 20 % over 2.8 s, the LFO's 55 % at 1/8, the 25 % chorus and 20 % reverb; estimated: the cutoff in hertz. Macro 1 (PWM) deepens the width's movement; Macro 2 (Bright) opens the filter; Macro 3 (Chorus) wets the chorus.

name: PWM Pop Lead
description: After Syntorial's recipe for a future-pop pluck lead: a quiet saw under a pulse an octave up two cents flat, two voices seventeen cents apart spread wide, mono gliding 20 ms, an 850 ms decay to nothing, the pulse width moved by a triangle in eighths, fully distorted, a small reverb. From the page: all of it; estimated: the cutoff in hertz. Macro 1 (Wobble) deepens the width's movement; Macro 2 (Decay) lets the notes ring longer; Macro 3 (Cutoff) opens the filter.

name: Screaming Sallen
description: A Sallen-Key pushed until it shrieks.

name: Shimmer Pulse Lead
description: After Syntorial's recipe for a bright progressive-house pulse lead: a 30 % pulse under a square an octave up that a fast triangle shakes by 28 cents, four voices thirteen cents apart, mono, a resonant low-pass following the keys a little, then an eighth-note echo and a reverb. From the page: the widths, levels, octave, unison, the 0/300/40 %/600 amp, the cutoff at 75 % with 35 % resonance and 20 % key tracking, the 1/16 shimmer, the echo's 20 % and 50 % feedback; estimated: the cutoff in hertz. Macro 1 (Shimmer) deepens the pitch shake; Macro 2 (Echo) brings up the delay.

name: Sirenengesang
description: Can be used as a substitute to human singing (high notes, monophonic) or a chill-inducing low frequency pad (low notes, chrods)

name: Square Lead
description: Two square-ish pulses, slightly apart.

name: Stepped Vibrato Lead
description: After Jon Musgrave's 8-bit sounds for MusicRadar: one square voice, mono, its vibrato a stepped triangle (sixteen steps, so it moves in jumps as a game console's did), its depth on the wheel. From the page: the single voice, the stepped-triangle vibrato and the wheel; estimated: the duty (a quarter), the rate and depth. Macro 1 (Vibrato) brings the stepped vibrato in; Macro 2 (Duty) narrows the pulse from a half to an eighth; Macro 3 (Bits) coarsens it.

name: Super Saw
description: Eight saws in classic unison, spread across the field.

name: Sync Lead
description: A hard-synced oscillator swept down by the mod envelope at each note.

name: Sync Sweep Lead
description: The sync table swept down by the second envelope at each note, gliding.

name: Talking Pulse Lead
description: After Syntorial's recipe for a talking pulse lead: a thin pulse two voices barely apart, in pulse-width warp, mono and legato with a short glide, through a very resonant, driven 24 dB low-pass near 520 Hz, soft-clipped, into a long reverb; moving the cutoff makes it speak. From the page: the thin pulse, the warp's 55 %, the glide's 21 ms, the cutoff, 80 % resonance and 20 % drive, the clip's 63 %, the reverb's 43 % at 2 s; estimated: our units for the warp. Macro 1 (Vowel), the page's mod wheel, sweeps the cutoff for the wah; Macro 2 (Space) widens the reverb.

name: Tech Trance Lead
description: After Syntorial's recipe for a driving tech-trance lead: one saw sixteen voices deep, detuned 43 % with its inner voices drawn in, through a 12 dB analog low-pass near 260 Hz that a triangle LFO in half notes sweeps, compressed hard, with a cut near 940 Hz, a lift above 3.4 kHz and a reverb. From the page: the voices, the detune and its power, the blend, the filter's cutoff, 10 % resonance and 12 % drive, the amp's 12/305/93 %/90, the LFO's 72 % to the cutoff, the EQ, the reverb's 37 % at 0.83 s; estimated: the turn into our units. Macro 1 (Motion) deepens the sweep; Macro 2 (Rate) doubles it toward quarters; Macro 3 (Space) widens the reverb.

name: Unison Saw Lead
description: Five detuned saws spread across the field.

name: Vowel Lead
description: The vowels table walked through by a slow LFO, as a voice says them.

name: Ambient Techno Pad
description: After Attack Magazine's ambient techno pads: a slow attack, a decay to just under full and a second's release, a 24 dB low-pass near 720 Hz and a high-pass near 280 Hz, a fast LFO on a synced table faded in over ten seconds (the longest rise here, for the page's twelve), a slow one on the sync and the cutoff, a wet ping-pong echo and a full reverb. From the page: the envelope's shape (its 5 s attack halved here so a chord blooms within a bar), the filters, the 13 Hz and 0.5 Hz LFOs and the 12 s fade, the echo's 50 % with 70 % feedback; estimated: our sync table for the page's sync, the reverb's mix. Macro 1 (Sync) deepens both LFOs; Macro 2 (Echo) the delay.

name: Bent PWM Pad
description: After Attack Magazine's wavetable pads: a pulse-width table nudged up by an envelope, its cycle bent by a warp an LFO moves, eight voices spread under half and detuned halfway, driven, a low cut and a gentle high shelf, into a bright hall. From the page: the envelope's 0.35 on the table, the bend at 40 % with the LFO's 0.46, the eight voices and 45 % spread, the drive, the EQ, the hall; estimated: the rates and our hall. Macro 1 (Bend) deepens the bend and the drive; Macro 2 (Space) widens the hall.

name: Blooming Pad
description: After Andy Jones's atmospheric pads for MusicRadar: two saws an octave apart and a little detuned, four voices each, a slow attack and long release, through a 12 dB low-pass high up that a sine LFO moves, into a long, damped reverb. From the page: the octave, the 1.03 detune, the four voices at 15, the amp's 22/50/92/81, the 12 dB cutoff near 90, the LFO; estimated: the times and the reverb. Macro 1 (Bloom) lengthens the attack and release and widens the reverb; Macro 2 (Cutoff) closes the filter.

name: Dark Drone
description: Low saws and a little noise, the cutoff breathing on the second LFO.

name: Dark Warm Pad
description: After Syntorial's recipe for a dark, warm pad: a saw and a medium pulse, seven voices each at 12 % detune spread full, through a nearly shut analog low-pass, a slow two-bar triangle and a fast flutter on the cutoff, a low cut and a dip near 262 Hz, a reverb. From the page: the levels (43 %, 54 %), voices and detune, the cutoff near 121 Hz with 4 % resonance, the amp's 219/711/90 %/372 ms, the two LFOs (15 % and 24 %), the EQ, the reverb's 45 % at 1.5 s; estimated: the cutoff raised to 320 Hz with a little key tracking to keep it heard, our detune. Macro 1 (Bright) opens the filter and deepens the flutter; Macro 2 (Space) widens the reverb.

name: Dreamy Eighties Pad
description: After Computer Music's dreamy eighties polysynth on MusicRadar: two saws an octave apart with noise at half, a gently resonant low-pass following the keys and opened a little by its envelope, a sine LFO wobbling both oscillators and the filter, chorus and a long reverb. From the page: the octave, the noise, the cutoff 25, resonance 20 and envelope 20, the envelopes (25/55/35/65 and 10/40/60/60), the LFO's rate and depth (12, 12); estimated: our units. Macro 1 (Drift) deepens the LFO; Macro 2 (Space) widens the reverb.

name: Dusty Drift Pad
description: After MusicRadar's dusty seventies pad from a modern synth: a saw in four voices and a square in eleven at 16 % detune, a near-full sustain and a long release, through a band-pass high up that an LFO drifts along with the noise, chorus and a little reverb. From the page: the voices and detune, the amp's 3/87/100/88, the band-pass at 92, the LFO near 35 on the cutoff and noise, the noise under half; estimated: our units. Macro 1 (Drift) deepens the LFO and adds a pitch drift; Macro 2 (Dust) brings the noise up.

name: Ensemble Saw Pad
description: After Computer Music's eighties pad in the style of a famous chorus-equipped polysynth (MusicRadar): a saw and its sub at seven tenths, a slow free LFO bending the pitch a little and moving the cutoff, the filter envelope turned upside down so each note dips, a slow attack and long release, chorus from mode I to both. From the page: the sub's 7, the LFO's rate near 0.3 and its small depths, the amp's 6/10/8/7, the cutoff 7, resonance 2, the inverted envelope at 3, the chorus; estimated: our units. Macro 1 (Ensemble) thickens the chorus and deepens the pitch LFO as mode I+II would; Macro 2 (Dip) deepens the inverted envelope.

name: Esoteric Soul Gathering
description: Created for my mom, those singing souls sound splendid!

name: Evolving Table Pad
description: After Joe Hanley's evolving pad for Syntorial: a unison table that a nine-second envelope walks through, an airy noise layer fading in over six seconds, a high, heavily detuned stack two octaves up chopped by a square LFO that rises in, a slow LFO on a gently resonant low-pass, chorus and a heavy reverb that breathes. From the page: the envelope's 9 s attack and decay to nothing on the position, the noise's 6 s attack, 8 s decay and 64 % sustain, the octaves, the six voices, the chopping LFO and its rise, the long release; estimated: the rates, the levels, the table. Macro 1 (Evolve) deepens the walk; Macro 2 (Air) brings the noise up; Macro 3 (Shimmer) the high stack.

name: Gated Supersaw Pad
description: After Attack Magazine's gated pad in the style of a famous electronic duo: two sixteen-voice saws, the second an octave up, through a 12 dB low-pass that a falling saw LFO opens on each cycle, a second LFO restarted at each note changing the first's rate so the gate stutters, a high-pass after it, an ensemble chorus and a small reverb. From the page: the voices and octave, the filters, the falling saw on the cutoff, the second LFO on the first's rate; estimated: the rates and depths. Macro 1 (Gate) deepens the gating; Macro 2 (Stutter) deepens the second LFO's hold on the first's rate.

name: Glass Choir
description: Vowels and a pulse an octave up, both moving slowly through their tables.

name: Glass Pad
description: A triangle and a thin pulse with a touch of FM, slowly moving.

name: Harmonic Drift
description: The harmonic build drifting on a slow LFO, its stacks spread through the table.

name: June Strings
description: June Bloom's DCO, a saw and a pulse in unison, through its own low-pass, a vibrato rising into each note.

name: Low-mid Simplicity
description: From Curiosity as part of the Forms Soundtrack

name: Macro Glass
description: A harmonic sweep through the pure filter's peak, drifting across the field; Macro 1 opens it, Macro 2 moves the table.

name: Overtone Drone Pad
description: After Nate Edwards's ambient pad for Attack Magazine: an overtone table eight voices deep two octaves down and a second an octave down, through a resonant low-pass its envelope opens and a resonant high-pass after it, a slow LFO on the high-pass, a stepped LFO walking the second table, the two LFOs together panning it. From the page: the octaves, the eight voices and their detunes (20 and 10), the resonances (60, 80), the envelopes' shapes, velocity on the cutoff, the stepped walk and the pan; estimated: our tables and every number. Macro 1 (Motion) deepens the walk and the pan; Macro 2 (Open) opens the low-pass.

name: Seasick Pad
description: After Syntorial's recipe for a breathing, slightly seasick pad: a saw four voices three cents apart with noise at 40 %, through a resonant low-pass following the keys, a slow attack and release, one bar-long triangle bending every voice's pitch by 56 cents together, a big, wet reverb. From the page: all of it; estimated: the cutoff in hertz. Macro 1 (Wow) deepens the pitch bend; Macro 2 (Noise) brings the noise up; Macro 3 (Space) widens the reverb.

name: Shimmer Noise
description: Noise spectra in shimmering unison, a little of the drawbars under it.

name: Shimmer Pad
description: A warm pad into the shimmer chain Paul White sets out in Sound On Sound: compressed so the tail stays dense, shifted an octave up and fed into a long hall with little damping. From the page: the order (compressor, octave shift, long undamped hall) and the compressor's ratio near 4:1 with a fast attack; designed: the pad and the amounts. Macro 1 (Shimmer) brings the octave shimmer up; Macro 2 (Size) lengthens the hall.

name: Smeared Vowel Pad
description: The vowels table read through the spectral smear, each partial held as the position walks slowly through the words, a second voice an octave down through a peak filter, wide and slow. Designed on the instrument to show the spectral morphs. Macro 1 (Smear) deepens the smear; Macro 2 (Vowel) moves through the table; Macro 3 (Space) widens the reverb.

name: String Machine
description: Bright saws in a wide ensemble, as a string machine plays.

name: Synth Choir
description: After Si Truss's string machine and synth choir for MusicRadar, its choir: a warm saw in ten voices at the usual detune through a formant filter with its resonance up, swept to an aah, a chaotic LFO nudging the voices' detune a hair as singers drift, chorus and reverb. From the page: the ten voices, the formant filter and its resonance, the chaos on the detune, the chorus and reverb; estimated: the vowel's place and our units. Macro 1 (Vowel) sweeps from aah toward ooh; Macro 2 (Ensemble) wets the chorus and deepens the drift.

name: Thin Pulse Air Pad
description: After Syntorial's recipe for a soft, band-limited pad: a thin pulse three voices barely detuned and not spread, a breath of white noise, through a low-pass near 552 Hz and a high-pass near 442 Hz that together make a band, both drifting on a two-second triangle, a chorus, a dip near 655 Hz and a reverb. From the page: all of it, the chorus's 41 % and the reverb's 43 %; estimated: our units, and the band widened (900 and 300 Hz) and the pulse a little wider so that it carries. Macro 1 (Air) widens the band and brings the noise up; Macro 2 (Chorus) wets the chorus.

name: Warm Pad
description: Detuned saws in unison that open slowly through the OTA cascade.

name: Washed Out Pad
description: After Nate Edwards's washed-out synths for Attack Magazine: a saw through a low-pass its envelope opens a little, into a band-pass, its tuning wobbling on a two-bar LFO, with a dotted-quarter echo on one side and a dotted half on the other. From the page: the filters and their places, the envelope's 25, the 2/1 LFO on the tuning at 10 to 20, the echoes' times; estimated: our units. Macro 1 (Wobble) deepens the tuning's wobble; Macro 2 (Echo) the delay; Macro 3 (Space) a reverb.

name: Hybrid Trap KickSnare
