description: Low notes for kick, high notes for SNARE!

description:
Mallet sound.

name: White Noise Hi-Hat
description: Basic but effective

name: Analog Pluck
description: A saw and a square an octave up, a fast filter envelope.

name: Digital Pluck
description: Bit steps swept toward the sine at each note, short.

name: Electro Saw Pluck
description: After Syntorial's recipe for an electro-house saw pluck: a saw four voices two cents apart started in phase, mono, a 200 ms decay to 70 %, a resonant low-pass whose envelope closes it over a second, an eighth-note echo and a medium reverb. From the page: all of it; estimated: the cutoff in hertz. Macro 1 (Bright) opens the filter and deepens its envelope; Macro 2 (Echo) the delay; Macro 3 (Space) the reverb.

name: Evolving Prog Pluck
description: After Syntorial's recipe for an evolving progressive-house lead: a triangle into a resonant, driven 24 dB low-pass that a sine in half notes moves, a saw an octave up brought in by a falling LFO in quarters that also moves a second low-pass, and a wide sixteen-voice sine brought in by a triangle in quarters, into a reverb. From the page: the oscillators and their LFOs (41 % to the first cutoff, 33 % and 40 % for the falling one, 72 % for the sine's level), the cutoffs near 127 and 166 Hz with their resonances (60 %, 33 %), the 90 ms release, the reverb's 44 %; estimated: our units. Macro 1 (Evolve) scales all three LFOs from still to fully pulsing; Macro 2 (Space) widens the reverb.

name: FM Bell
description: Two sines a fifth and an octave apart, the FM fading with the note.

name: FM Euro Pluck
description: After Syntorial's recipe for a soft eurodance FM pluck: a triangle bent by a silent pulse at half depth, a triangle sub an octave down, a 550 ms decay, a shut, resonant low-pass thrown fully open by a 250 ms envelope, velocity on the level, a quarter-note echo and a big reverb. From the page: all of it, the echo's 25 % with 50 % feedback and the 50 % reverb; estimated: our units for the FM. Macro 1 (Bite) deepens the FM; Macro 2 (Cutoff) opens the filter; Macro 3 (Space) the reverb.

name: Fold Pluck
description: The wavefold struck hard and settling back to its sine.

name: Kalimba Pluck
description: After Syntorial's recipe for a woody FM pluck: a sine bent by a silent sine two octaves up (four times its pitch), the bend only on a 250 ms envelope, four voices in tune spread full, started in phase, high-passed, fully wet slow chorus and a reverb. From the page: the ratio, the 0/250/0 envelope at full depth, the amp's 0/100 %/220, the unison, the high-pass at 60 %, the chorus and the 20 % reverb, velocity on the level; estimated: our units. Macro 1 (Mallet) turns soft rubber into hard wood, deepening and lengthening the bend; Macro 2 (Space) widens the reverb.

name: Marimba Pluck
description: After ADSR Sounds' tropical marimba pluck: a table swept from bright to sine over the first 350 ms by a one-shot, a quantized two-frame layer a little quieter beside it, a noise click past the filter, a one-second decay, a gently resonant low-pass near 7.5 kHz, a slow chorus, compression, a quarter-note echo low in the mix and a hall. From the page: the sweep's 300 to 400 ms, the amp's 1/1000/0/100, the 40 % quantize, the noise attack, the filter, the effects' amounts (chorus near 60 %, the hall at 25 to 30 % size); estimated: our tables. Macro 1 (Mallet) starts the sweep brighter and the click louder; Macro 2 (Space) widens the hall.

name: Noise Saw Pluck
description: After Reverb Machine's lo-fi retrowave set with Forhill: noise just under half beside a full saw, a high-pass before a low-pass its envelope plucks, the pan swept by an LFO a bar long, a ping-pong echo a quarter on one side and a half on the other. From the page: the levels, the filter order, the bar-long pan LFO, the ping-pong's times; estimated: the cutoffs and decays. Macro 1 (Noise) brings the noise up; Macro 2 (Cutoff) opens the low-pass; Macro 3 (Echo) the ping-pong.

name: Pizzicato Blip Pluck
description: After Syntorial's recipe for a pizzicato trance pluck: a narrow pulse and a half-width pulse an octave up, a triangle sub an octave down, each note's pitch blipping down from three octaves up in 20 ms, a resonant low-pass plucked by a 250 ms envelope, a quarter-note echo and a big reverb. From the page: the oscillators and levels (50 %, 50 %, 45 %), the 10/100 %/15 ms amp, the cutoff at 40 % with 45 % resonance, the envelope's 50 %, the +3 octave blip, the echo's 25 % with 50 % feedback, the 30 % reverb; estimated: the cutoff in hertz. Macro 1 (Snap) deepens the blip; Macro 2 (Cutoff) opens the filter; Macro 3 (Space) the reverb.

name: Retro Night Pluck
description: After Reverb Machine's breakdown of a synthwave night-call track, its plucked arpeggio: a saw with no sub, a high-pass under a gently resonant low-pass that a plucky envelope opens, the keys not followed, a chorus, an ensemble at a third, a light echo and a little down-sampling, lifted near 3 and 5.3 kHz. From the page: the filters (8.37 and 4.53 on that synth, resonance 2.42, envelope 2.77, no key tracking), the slight attack, the effects; estimated: their units here. Macro 1 (Pluck) shortens and deepens the envelope; Macro 2 (Ensemble) wets the chorus; Macro 3 (Echo) the delay.

name: Soft Uplifting Pluck
description: After a KVR forum thread on a soft, heavenly uplifting-trance pluck: saws stacked at the note and one and two octaves down, a low cutoff with moderate resonance plucked by a short envelope with no sustain, compressed, saturated and reverberant. From the thread: the stacked octaves, the filter and envelope, the heavy compression, saturation and reverb, and its tip that raising the envelope's sustain turns the pluck into a lead, and that one knob should open the cutoff while lowering the resonance; estimated: every number. Macro 1 (Open) opens the cutoff and lowers the resonance; Macro 2 (Sustain) raises the sustain toward a lead.

name: Trance Arp Pluck
description: After Syntorial's recipe for a classic trance arp pluck: two half-width pulses an octave apart (80 % and 20 %), two voices two cents apart spread full, a 350 ms decay to nothing, a low-pass at a quarter that a 300 ms envelope opens by 45 %, and the dotted-eighth ping-pong and medium reverb the page suggests adding. From the page: the oscillators, unison, envelopes and filter; estimated: the effects and the cutoff in hertz. Macro 1 (Length) lengthens both decays; Macro 2 (Cutoff) opens the filter; Macro 3 (Echo) brings up the ping-pong.

name: Transient Stack Pluck
description: After Cymatics' step-by-step guide to plucks: two oscillators a few cents either side of the note, each stacked an octave up, a 20 ms transient on the pitch, a quick decay, and a big reverb gated short after it. From the page: the pitch transient's 20 ms, the octave stack, the few cents (never past 30), the gated reverb; estimated: the rest, the gate made here by a short decay. Macro 1 (Transient) deepens the pitch flick; Macro 2 (Gate) lets the reverb's tail through.

name: Acid Step Arp
description: After Attack Magazine's acid line from a synth's step arpeggiator: a pulse two octaves down, sixteenths with a short gate, a 12 dB low-pass with some resonance and drive that a modulation envelope opens, legato glide, a fold-back distortion half wet. From the page: the pulse at -2 octaves, the 1/16 rate and 18 % gate, the cutoff near 4/10, resonance 3.25 and drive 2, the envelope's 7.3 with its decay 3.8 and sustain 1.7, the glide at half, the fold at 50 %; estimated: our units, an up-and-down shape for the page's drawn steps. Macro 1 (Cutoff) opens the filter; Macro 2 (Squelch) raises the resonance and the envelope together; Macro 3 (Fold) wets the fold.

name: Bell Loop Sequence
description: After Attack Magazine's hypnotic techno sequence: a dirty saw shut down and plucked by its envelope, a triangle an octave up through its own resonant filter faded in as the page's XY pad does, a synced LFO warbling the tuning, a wide echo; here played by the arpeggiator over the held chord. From the page: the saw through a shut filter with its envelope near 4 o'clock and driven input, the triangle's octave and its filter (12 and 3 o'clock), the warble, the echo; estimated: our units. Macro 1 (Layer) brings the triangle layer in; Macro 2 (Pluck) deepens the saw's envelope; Macro 3 (Echo) the delay.

name: Berlin Sequence
description: After Computer Music's Berlin school sequence on MusicRadar: a warm saw and a pulse through the transistor ladder, a plucky envelope with no sustain, up and down two octaves in sixteenths, a slow LFO breathing in the cutoff as a hand on the knob would, a synced echo. From the page: the saw and pulse, the ladder, the envelope's decay and release with no sustain, the synced echo; estimated: the echo's dotted eighth for the page's six eighths, the LFO and the numbers. Macro 1 (Cutoff) opens it; Macro 2 (Resonance) makes it ring; Macro 3 (Echo) feeds the delay.

name: Bit Step Arp
description: The bit-steps table in its coarsest steps, up three octaves in thirty-seconds as a game's chord arpeggio. Macro 1 (Bits) walks from coarse steps back toward the sine; Macro 2 (Echo) brings up a short echo.

name: Chord Pulse Arp
description: The whole chord struck on every eighth by the arpeggiator, saws a little apart through a plucked filter: a rhythm made of the chord. Macro 1 (Cutoff) opens it; Macro 2 (Length) lets the chords ring; Macro 3 (Space) brings up the reverb.

name: Converging Bells
description: Bell tones of a sine bent by a second sine two octaves and a fifth up, stepping in from the chord's outer notes in sixteenths. Macro 1 (Metal) deepens the FM; Macro 2 (Space) widens the reverb.

name: Drifting Dream Arp
description: A soft triangle stepping up and down at random in eighths, each note slow to fade, into a long hall and a dotted echo. Macro 1 (Tone) brightens it toward a saw; Macro 2 (Space) deepens the hall; Macro 3 (Echo) feeds the delay.

name: Gated Sequence
description: After Roland Schmidt's gated synth sequence for MusicRadar: a held chord chopped into a rhythm by a sixteen-step LFO in sixteenths on a driven low-pass and a falling saw in sixteenths on the volume. From the page: the filter's 89 cutoff, 10 resonance and 23 drive, the stepped LFO's 32 to the cutoff, the falling saw's 62 to the volume, the amp's 0/50/80/30; estimated: our units and the steps. Macro 1 (Gate) deepens the volume chop, from a smooth pad to a choppy gate; Macro 2 (Steps) deepens the stepped filter.

name: Hypnotic Table Arp
description: The FM table's middle played in the order the keys were struck, its position wandering on a slow LFO so the loop never repeats the same. Macro 1 (Morph) moves the table; Macro 2 (Resonance) sharpens the band-pass; Macro 3 (Echo) brings up the delay.

name: Melodic Triplet Arp
description: After Attack Magazine's melodic arpeggios: a saw up and down in eighth-note triplets, gliding between steps, the filter shut and opened fully by a short envelope, a chorus, an eighth-note echo and a reverb near 2.7 s. From the page: the shape and rate, the glide's 19, the amp's 30/0/32, the cutoff at zero with the envelope at full (0/31/0/36), the chorus, the echo, the reverb's 6.5 ms pre-delay and 2.72 s; estimated: our units. Macro 1 (Bright) opens the filter and brings the echo up, as the page's cutoff ride does; Macro 2 (Glide) lengthens the slide.

name: Random Glass Arp
description: Sine-bright glass from the sync table, notes picked at random over three octaves in sixteenths, ringing into a long hall. Macro 1 (Shine) moves the table into its brighter syncs; Macro 2 (Space) widens the hall.

name: Retro Octave Arp
description: A clocked oscillator's saw and pulse up an octave and back in sixteenths, through its own low-pass and a wide chorus, as the eighties sequencers ran. Macro 1 (Bright) opens the filter; Macro 2 (Chorus) widens it; Macro 3 (Decay) lengthens each step.

name: Step Pluck Sequence
description: After Roland Schmidt's patch built on a synth's own sequencer for MusicRadar: a phase-distorted square and saw through a gentle 6 dB-style low-pass, both envelopes plucking each step, the filter's fully open, run here by the arpeggiator, with an echo at low feedback. From the page: the oscillators, the low cutoff, the amp's 1/32/0/24 and the filter's 10/34/0/33 at full depth, the echo; estimated: our tables for its phase distortion, the arpeggio for its steps. Macro 1 (Decay) lengthens both envelopes; Macro 2 (Cutoff) opens the filter.

name: Swung Retro Bass Arp
description: After Simon Mitchell's retro basslines for Attack Magazine: a folded table and a saw an octave down, fine-tuned eight cents apart either way, sixteenths with half a gate and 55 % swing, a resonant low-pass its envelope opens, half-note and quarter-note LFOs moving the shapes, a dark chorus, a tape drive and heavy compression. From the page: the octave, the fines, the arp's rate, gate and swing, the cutoff 42, resonance 30 and envelope 40, the LFOs, the chorus's 35 % and the drive's 20 %, the page's two macros (the first tone and shape, the second compression and drive); estimated: our tables. Macro 1 (Tone) moves the table and its fold; Macro 2 (Crunch) pushes the drive and the compression.

name: Sync Arp Bass
description: A synced saw low down, the arpeggio rising an octave in sixteenths as a driving bass sequence, the sync swept by each step's envelope. Macro 1 (Sync) sweeps the sync higher; Macro 2 (Cutoff) opens the filter.

name: Trance Gate Arp
description: Saws in a five-voice stack, run up two octaves in sixteenths with a short gate, each step plucked open by the filter and echoed on the dotted eighth. Macro 1 (Cutoff) opens the filter; Macro 2 (Length) lets each step ring longer; Macro 3 (Echo) brings up the delay.

name: Vintage Unison Arp
description: After Attack Magazine's vintage arpeggio: a four-voice oscillator an octave down and a five-voice saw a hair detuned, a plucked amp, sixteenths with a short gate, a warm-driven 24 dB low-pass nearly shut and thrown open by a full envelope, a chaotic LFO drifting the pitch, velocity on the cutoff. From the page: the octave and voices, the arp's 1/16 and 30 % gate, the low-pass's drive 2.1 and resonance 2, the full envelope, the chaotic LFO at 8/1T on the pitch, velocity's 1.14; estimated: our units. Macro 1 (Cutoff) opens the filter; Macro 2 (Drift) deepens the chaos on the pitch; Macro 3 (Decay) lengthens each step.

name: Divide-Down Strings
description: After Si Truss's string machine for MusicRadar: two narrow pulses an octave apart through a low-pass near 6 kHz and a high-pass near 200 Hz, full sustain with a soft attack and long release, through two choruses, the second set a little apart from the first, as the old ensemble boxes did. From the page: the pulses (5 to 20 % wide), the octave, the filters, the envelope's shape, the two choruses; estimated: the times and the choruses' settings. Macro 1 (Ensemble) deepens and wets the first chorus; Macro 2 (Attack) slows the bow.

name: Night Drive Strings
description: After Reverb Machine's synthwave breakdown of a night-drive soundtrack, its strings: one saw in unison through a low-pass shut down near 66 Hz with no key tracking, opened by an envelope with a 68 ms attack, a decay over 1.2 s to three quarters, a chorus, an echo at a quarter of the mix and a half-wet reverb. From the page: the saw, the cutoff, the envelope's 5.16 and its 68/1200/74 %, the chorus, the 25 % echo and 50 % reverb; estimated: our envelope depth. Macro 1 (Swell) slows the envelope's attack and deepens it; Macro 2 (Space) widens the reverb.

name: Pulse Saw Strings
description: After Reverb Machine's breakdown of a synthwave night-call track, its strings: a saw and an 85 % pulse twelve cents apart through a low-pass near 280 Hz whose envelope swells in over 44 ms and falls over five and a half seconds, into a chorus. From the page: the waves, the twelve cents, the cutoff, the 44 ms and 5.4 s, the chorus; estimated: the envelope's depth. Macro 1 (Open) opens the filter; Macro 2 (Chorus) wets the chorus.

name: Section Strings
description: After Syntorial's recipe for a bright unison string pad: a saw in four voices at 16 % detune, the outer ones low against the middle and spread 38 %, the low-pass fully open, a 25 ms attack, a decay to 85 % and a release over six and a half seconds, a slow four-voice chorus and a little reverb. From the page: all of it, the chorus's 0.11 Hz and 27 %, the reverb's 13 %; estimated: our detune, and poly play where the recipe is mono. Macro 1 (Section) widens the detune and the chorus from a solo toward a full section; Macro 2 (Release) shortens the release for faster lines.

name: Tape Strings
description: After Roland Schmidt's tape-inspired string patch for MusicRadar: two saws tuned a little apart either way, stereo white noise, through a band-pass its envelope opens, slow attacks on both envelopes, and a smooth random LFO bending the two saws in opposite directions as a stretched tape would. From the page: the detunes (+4, -3), the noise's 38, the band-pass at 28 with the envelope's 61, the envelopes (47/50/80/8 and 62/50/80/8), the random LFO's 26 to the tunings, +2 and -2; estimated: our units. Macro 1 (Wow) deepens the opposite bends; Macro 2 (Air) brings the noise up.
